wwo.name: Moscow
wwo.method: 1897 city plan traced at four frozen locations. Kitay-Gorod and Red Square connect across period crossings to the Zamoskvorechye street grid. The western segment follows Nikitskaya and Presnya to river land uses. Myasnitskaya leads to the three terminals, historical Red Pond and the Sokolniki approach. Road widths, surfaces, individual parcel dimensions and building heights are display estimates. Untraced streets retain the fallback. River-channel widths outside the trace, exact cadastral layouts, complete industrial boundaries and measured historic terrain remain unresolved.

registration.reference: Eight overlapping windows from the same 1897 EtoMesto registered Trofimov/Ilyin city plan, viewer map 7996. WGS84 longitude and latitude are interpolated between the viewer grid lines bordering each map pixel. No survey accuracy is claimed.
registration.precision_limit: The alignment relies on the source viewer. The landmarks identify the sheet and local registrations approximately. No independent adjustment or validated residual is available.

sources.title: Plan of Moscow, city survey of A. N. Trofimov, A. Ilyin Cartographic Establishment
sources.licence: Historical 1897 print. EtoMesto images kept in local research storage under its stated use terms. Distributed geometry is an original historical redrawing.
sources.precision: The selected original map shows street axes, water, station layout, land-use enclosures and some roof plans. It does not give detailed parcels, metric widths, roof heights, or paving materials.

sources.title: Moscau II. Innere Stadt, Baedeker Russland, fourth edition
sources.publisher: Karl Baedeker, Leipzig. Catalogue scan from Retromap.
sources.licence: Historical 1897 print consulted for plan identities. Reference pixels excluded.
sources.precision: Inner city, named core crossings and street hierarchy corroboration. Primary geometry comes from the Trofimov/Ilyin sheet.

properties.basis: Pond shape enclosed by the field lanes and filled with historic water hatching.
Second mapped field pond at the Trekhgornaya approach.
Open courts between the marked palace and service blocks, inside the historic Kremlin perimeter.
Period Bolotnaya open market space on the island, bounded by the visible street and canal.
Part of the labelled excise yard beside the water. The exact uses inside the enclosure are unknown.
Mapped cathedral outline at the southern end of Red Square. The display height collapses the historical cluster of unequal towers into a single mass.
Selected range of the mapped Upper Trading Rows, within the full historic market block. Display massing is estimated.
Main visible portion of the perimeter Arsenal range. Simplified roof mass. The other wings are outside this footprint.
Compact main Historical Museum outline at the northwest entrance to Red Square. Display height is approximate.
Mapped St Clement outline and 18th-century church corroboration. The display mass uses an approximate height.
Conservative outline of the church near the north river embankment. Approximate height.
Building range drawn at the Nikolaevsky terminus. Station use is corroborated by the city transport archive.
The mapped Yaroslavsky terminal portion near the Red Pond. Form and height are approximate.
Selected Moscow–Ryazan terminal range shown in 1897. The later Kazansky Station envelope is excluded.
Mapped building range in the labelled brewery on the bank opposite the Presnya quarry. Display height and individual production use are approximate.
Conservative outline of the Studenets estate house as printed by the river garden. Approximate display height.
One marked building above the labelled wine excise ground. Display mass and individual interior allocation are approximate.
